featured_reviews.name: Ms.Dear369
featured_reviews.review_text:
Today, during my visit to Mumbai, I had the pleasure of dining once again at Dakshin Garden Bar & Kitchen. This was my second time here, and once again, the experience was outstanding. I ordered the pomfret fish, tiger prawns, and mushroom tikka. Each dish was bursting with authentic flavors, and I especially appreciated that the kitchen adjusted the spice level to my preference—it made the food even more delicious and perfectly suited to my taste. The spices were bold and aromatic, truly showcasing the richness of Indian cuisine.

The atmosphere was warm and relaxing, while the staff were attentive, friendly, and made sure everything was just right. Every dish was cooked to perfection and full of flavor. Without a doubt, I will be returning on my next trip to Mumbai to enjoy this wonderful dining experience again.

featured_reviews.name: Darshak Uchil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Dakshin recently. The ambience and overall setup were good, and the restaurant has a nice fine-dining feel. The food quality was decent with authentic South Indian flavors, though a few dishes felt slightly overpriced for the portion size.

Service was polite but a bit slow during peak hours. Overall, it was a satisfactory experience — good for trying traditional South Indian cuisine in a premium setting, but there is still some scope for improvement in service speed and value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Shobha's Kitchen
featured_reviews.review_text:
Worst food and customer service experience ever from Dakshin.

Ordered Chicken Tandoori and received something that didn’t even look fresh or properly cooked. The food quality was extremely poor and looked completely unappetizing. When we contacted the restaurant for help, the staff behaved very rudely, spoke arrogantly, and kept delaying the issue for hours.

Instead of resolving the complaint, they kept saying “wait” and later started arguing and blaming us. The manager’s response was shocking — saying that they serve everyone the same way and nobody has complained of food poisoning. Such careless and insensitive behavior towards customers is unacceptable.

Very disappointing experience overall. Poor food quality, rude staff, and zero accountability.

featured_reviews.name: Pinkart
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing and disgusting experience with Dakshin.
We had ordered Chicken Tandoori but received something completely different. The food looked stale, burnt, and honestly so bad that it felt nauseating even looking at it. After contacting the restaurant, instead of helping us, the staff spoke very arrogantly on the call, shouted at us, and kept making us wait for over 2 hours saying they were “checking with the delivery partner.”
When we called again after waiting, the manager casually said, “Sabko hum aise hi dete hai” and started blaming us instead. Their response was basically that “everyone eats it like this” and “nobody got food poisoning,” which is an absolutely irresponsible thing to say to a customer raising a food quality concern.
Very unprofessional behavior, zero customer service, and extremely concerning food quality. Definitely not ordering again.

featured_reviews.review_text:

Recently visited this amazing place located in Santacruz, hands down one of the best places for South Indian food items. The ambience is really calm and soothing. This place can accommodate a huge crowd, the food was excellent, all of the dishes were served fresh and well prepared.

featured_reviews.name: Invincible Crown
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dakshin bar and kitchen offers variety of veg and non veg dishes best known for their fish and chicken variety
Its a dim lit place very soothing ,spacious with beautiful planters around .You will also find sports screening  on tv.Come alone with friends,family they have indoor as well as outdoor seating ! They have a bar counter with refreshing mocktails and cocktails .
Listing few of their dishes which we relished
So for starters we tried their VEG KINALE which was like bread pockets filled with creamy stuffing fried so it was crispy kids enjoyed it with ketchup. Then we tried their HARI MIRCH PRAWNS though the name sounds spicy but it was perfectly cooked prawns with just the right amount of spices must try .
Then for the main course we had their MALABAR CHICKEN GRAVY it was made typical authentic style and tasted well with appam we almost slurped the gravy down it was so delicious .
Then we ordered mocktails VIRGIN MOJITO and MOJITO BLUE LAGOON both were refreshing
Finally we ordered BROWNIE with ICECREAM for dessert .
It was our best experience if you are around santacruz do visit it once !

featured_reviews.name: Divya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dumpling Khang is a place I’ve been going to since 2019 — I still remember the first time I tried their chicken thupka and how much I absolutely loved it. It had this authentic, comforting flavour that made me come back again and again. For a long time, I used to order their momo-thupka combo on a monthly basis — and back then it felt totally worth it. It was around ₹170, came with a generous bowl of soup and 6 momos, and tasted super fresh.

Over time, of course, the price went up (₹190… ₹200… and now it’s ₹320-350 if you order online), but what’s more disappointing is that the quality has definitely gone down. The thupka still hits on some days, but the momos have become really average — they taste like pre-packed ones just deep-fried and served. Not the fresh, soft, flavourful momos they used to be.

There’s also this dish called Laughing — which they hype up quite a bit — but honestly, it was very underwhelming. It’s basically some kind of roll (reminded me of Gujarati khaman) with Maggi/Wai Wai noodles stuffed inside, and that’s it. For the price, it really doesn’t deliver.

We also tried their Nepali thali on our recent visit — again, something they highly recommended. But that was another miss. It had rice, basic dal, some greens, one sabzi (usually an aloo sabzi), a small portion of chicken gravy and achar. It was okay, not bad, but definitely not something I’d go back for.

Now coming to the space itself — it’s tiny. Like, four tables tiny. So only four groups (of 3–4 people max) can sit at a time. Because of that, if you go during peak hours, it gets super crowded and you may have to wait. And even after placing your order, the food can take a while to arrive. That said, the place does give off a very warm, comforting, homely vibe. It’s the kind of small place that makes you want to curl up with soup on a rainy day.

They also usually do these combo offers during New Year and other festivals — where you get a set number of dishes or momos for a fixed price. I’d honestly recommend that more than dining in right now. The combos are way more reasonable and they get delivered to your home, so you skip the waiting and the crowd.

So yeah — if you’ve never tried it, go for their soups. They still remind me of the flavours from Himachal. But otherwise, the rest of the food is average, prices are high now, and the overall experience just isn’t what it used to be.

featured_reviews.name: Rishikesh Verma
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imlee – The Chaat Gali offers a modern twist on traditional Indian street food in the heart of Bandra. The ambiance is chic and inviting, providing a comfortable setting for chaat enthusiasts.  ￼

Food:
The menu showcases a variety of regional chaats, including Pani Puri, Bhel Puri, and Aloo Tikki, each prepared with a contemporary flair. While the use of fresh ingredients is evident, some dishes might benefit from bolder flavors to capture the authentic street food essence.  ￼

Service:
The staff is attentive and ensures a pleasant dining experience. However, during peak hours, service can be slightly delayed due to high demand.

Value for Money:
Considering the upscale ambiance and quality ingredients, the pricing is reasonable. It’s a great spot for those looking to enjoy street food in a more refined environment. ￼

Overall Experience:
Imlee is a commendable attempt to elevate traditional chaats for a modern audience. While there’s room for enhancing the authenticity of flavors, it’s worth a visit for those seeking a unique chaat experience in Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Noel Rodriques
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you love street food, Imlee - The Chaat Galli is a must-visit! 🌟
Their Pani Puri cart is magic — imagine tasting Delhi ke Golgappe, Kolkata ke Puchka, and Mumbai ki Pani Puri all at one place! Each one was fresh, crispy, and full of flavour.h

We also tried their Dahi Bhalle and Papdi Chaat — both were loaded with dahi and perfectly balanced masalas. The Cheese Pav Bhaji was rich, creamy, and super satisfying.

And to end on a sweet note — the Meerut ki Jalebi totally stole the show! Crispy, juicy, and just the right amount of sweetness.

The place has a lovely ambiance where you can actually sit and enjoy your street food cravings in comfort. Highly recommend this spot for chaat lovers in the city!

✅ Tip: Don’t miss the Pani Puri cart experience — it’s fun and delicious!

featured_reviews.name: Sneha
featured_reviews.review_text:
At Imlee, Santacruz, we recently tried a few things. We started with three varieties of everyon’s favourite - Panipuri, Golgappa and Puchka. Then we had Dilli ki famous Rani Kachori Chaat which was highly recommended by Curly Tales. Honestly, I had never eaten this inspite of many trips to Delhi.  Then we had Agra ke Matar Poori our Kacche Tamatar ki Sabji.
Kadhi Chawal from Haridwar ki Gali was another staff recommendation. This kinda took me back to the Kadhi chawal from Chotiwala in Rishikesh. Simple and perfect!
We finished our meal with Ras Malai.
There were many more items on the menu. All regional street food from North and Central India. Everything we ate here left us wanting more. The staff’s recommendations were on point. This is Imlee by Neeti Goel & Curly Tales, a cute place where you have your favourite street food under one roof. Check it out.

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Upadhyay

Every dish I tried was lipsmacking and delicious—from the tangy chaats to spicy snacks, the flavors are just spot-on. It’s like the best of Indian streets served up in a trendy, clean, and super fun setting. 😋✨

What really stood out? The ambience. It’s not just a restaurant, it’s an experience. Think colorful, energetic, and full of character—perfect for catching up with friends, clicking some aesthetic pics, or simply enjoying great food with a side of great vibes.

featured_reviews.name: Prathamesh Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Had an amazing experience at Chaat Hauz in Khar! As someone who loves chaat, it's rare to find a place that gets every dish right, but this place absolutely delivered.
We started with the Palak Patta Chaat, and it was outstanding. The crispy spinach leaves, perfectly balanced chutneys, and crunchy toppings created an explosion of flavors and textures in every bite. Easily one of the best versions I've had in Mumbai.
The Ragda Pattice was equally impressive. The pattice was crisp on the outside and soft inside, while the ragda was flavorful and comforting without being overly spicy. It had that authentic street-food taste with a premium touch.
The Dahi Makhana Chaat was a pleasant surprise and probably the most unique dish of the lot. Light, refreshing, and beautifully balanced with creamy dahi and flavorful chutneys, it stood out from the usual chaat options available elsewhere.
The star of the evening was the Avocado Papdi Chaat. Such a creative fusion dish! The creamy avocado blended beautifully with the traditional chaat elements, creating something innovative without losing the essence of authentic Indian chaat.
The presentation of every dish was excellent, ingredients tasted fresh, portions were satisfying, and the service was warm and attentive. The restaurant has managed to give traditional chaat a modern twist while maintaining authentic flavors.
If you're a chaat lover looking for something beyond the ordinary, Chaat Hauz in Khar is definitely worth visiting. Every dish we tried was packed with flavor, creativity, and quality. Looking forward to coming back and exploring more of their menu. Highly recommended! 🌟🌟🌟🌟🌟

featured_reviews.name: Zakiya Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text: QFinally found the best chaat spot in Khar and Chaat Hauz completely lives up to the hype — every single item is a flavour bomb and you can taste the freshness in every bite. Started with their legendary pani puri where the puris were perfectly crisp and the teekha-khatta pudina pani had that perfect street-style kick that hits instantly, then moved to dahi batata puri which was insanely balanced with chilled sweet dahi, tangy chutneys, and aloo masala that just melts in your mouth without making the puri soggy at all. The sev puri had great crunch with fresh onion-tomato toppings and the ragda pattice was piping hot with buttery ragda, spicy chutneys, and loads of sev on top — proper Mumbai style. Even though it’s a small standing/takeaway setup with no seating, the counters are surprisingly clean, staff is super quick even during the 6-9pm rush, and hygiene is clearly a priority which is rare for street chaat places. Prices are very reasonable at ₹60-120 per plate and portions are generous, plus the bhaiya serving is polite and remembers regulars. If you’re craving authentic, no-nonsense Mumbai chaat that tastes exactly like it should, skip the fancy cafes and come straight here — Chaat Hauz is a Khar institution for a reason and I’m already planning my next visit for bhel and samosa chaat!

Everything arrived fresh, flavourful and well-packed, with the packaging ensuring the food stayed intact during delivery. The order was delivered on time, and the quality was impressive from start to finish. A satisfying chaat craving, sorted right at home!
